newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere keeps surging in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere keeps surging in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere ploughed ahead holding its surge past a 20-month barrier at $13.125 on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Monday.
The BLOM general index climbed 3.93 percent to hit a record 1117.04. The LISPI general index increased 15.96 percent to hit 94.80.
Market turnover was 306,783 shares for a value of $3,914,873 against Friday's 354,420 shares for a value of $4,743,022.
Solidere A hit $13.1250, its highest level since August of 1995 and Solidere B reached $13.1250, its highest point since September of 1995.
Last Thursday's news that Solidere planned to open up share ownership to foreign investors in October fuelled a surge by the company's A and B shares.
Banque Audi reached $28, down from Friday's record $28.5.
Audi last week announced the acquisition for $50 million of medium-sized Credit Commercial du Moyen-Orient which has assets of $253 million.
Bank of Beirut climbed to a record high of $4.6250 from $4.5. Bank Libanaise pour le Commerce fell to $20.5 from Friday's $20.75.
There was no trade in the three other industrial firms: Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic.
